891	   * The argument retry, for a call that no attempt keeps, an argument of
892	   * which is itself a call whose static args it inferred with no expected
893	   * type. Each candidate in turn: each such argument is checked again with
894	   * the candidate's parameter type at its position as its expected type, that
895	   * type instantiated, where the candidate has static parameters, by the other
896	   * arguments (writesStaticArgs) and the call's expected type alone; the call is then checked
897	   * against that candidate alone, and the candidate counts when the call's
898	   * type converts to the expected type. Of the candidates that count, the one
899	   * more specific on its declared parameter types than every other is kept,
900	   * with its arguments. Otherwise the call is refused as it was.
901	   */
902	  private def retypedApplication(preCandidates: List[PreAppCandidate],
903	                                 iargs: List[Expr],
904	                                 args: List[Either[Expr, FnExpr]],
905	                                 context: Option[Type],
906	                                 mOpName: Option[Op],
907	                                 fallBackWithoutContext: Boolean)
908	                                (implicit errorFactory: ApplicationErrorFactory)
909	                                 : Option[(List[AppCandidate], Type)] = {
910	    val positions = args.zipWithIndex.collect { case (Left(c), i) if retypable(c) => i }.toSet
911	    if (positions.isEmpty || iargs.size != args.size) return None
912	    val tryChecker = STypeCheckerFactory.makeTryChecker(this)
913	    def same(a: Expr, b: Expr) = Formula.isTrue(analyzer.equivalent(getType(a).get, getType(b).get))
914	    val found = preCandidates.flatMap { pc =>
915	      val domain =
916	        if (!hasStaticParams(pc.arrow)) Some(pc.arrow.getDomain)
917	        else {
918	          val tys = args.zipWithIndex.map {
919	            case (Left(e), i) if !positions(i) || writesStaticArgs(iargs(i)) => Some(getType(e).get)
920	            case _ => None
921	          }
922	          def constraint(inf: ArrowType, ops: Map[Op, Op]): CFormula =
923	            Formula.and(context.map(c => analyzer.subtype(inf.getRange, c)).toList ++
924	                        zipWithDomain(tys, inf.getDomain).collect { case (Some(t), d) => analyzer.subtype(t, d) })
925	          inferStaticParamsHelper(pc.arrow, constraint, false, true, true).map(_._1.getDomain)
926	        }
927	      domain.toList.flatMap { dom =>
928	        val params = zipWithDomain(args, dom).map(_._2)
929	        val newArgs = args.zipWithIndex.map {
930	          case (Left(c), i) if positions(i) && i < params.size && !hasInferenceVars(params(i)) =>
931	            Left(tryChecker.tryCheckExpr(iargs(i), Some(params(i))).filter(!same(_, c)).getOrElse(c))
932	          case (a, _) => a
933	        }
934	        if (newArgs.zip(args).forall { case (n, o) => n eq o }) Nil
935	        else (try {
936	          tryChecker.typedApplicationOfChecked(List(pc), iargs, newArgs, context, mOpName,
937	                                               fallBackWithoutContext, false)
938	        } catch { case _: StaticError => None }).
939	          filter(r => context.forall(coercions.substitutableFor(r._2, _))).toList.map(r => (pc, r))
940	      }
941	    }
942	    def better(a: (PreAppCandidate, (List[AppCandidate], Type)), b: (PreAppCandidate, (List[AppCandidate], Type))) =
943	      (a eq b) || moreSpecificCandidate(a._2._1.head, b._2._1.head, Some(a._1.arrow), Some(b._1.arrow))
944	    found.filter(a => found.forall(better(a, _))) match {
945	      case List(best) => Some((best._2._1 ++ found.filterNot(_ eq best).map(_._2._1.head), best._2._2))

947	    }

952	   * static args. Where they are written, the check again gives the same
953	   * type, and the retry passes over the argument.
954	   */
955	  private def retypable(c: Expr): Boolean = c match {
956	    case S_RewriteFnApp(_, f: FunctionalRef, _) => !f.getStaticArgs.isEmpty
957	    case SOpExpr(_, f, _) => !f.getStaticArgs.isEmpty
958	    case m: MethodInvocation => !m.getStaticArgs.isEmpty

964	   * mk[\ZZ64\]() does. Such an argument instantiates a generic candidate in
965	   * the retry as any other argument does.

967	  private def writesStaticArgs(e: Expr): Boolean = e match {
968	    case SJuxt(_, _, _, front::_, _, true) => writesStaticArgs(front)
969	    case SMathPrimary(_, _, _, front, _) => writesStaticArgs(front)
970	    case S_RewriteFnApp(_, f, _) => writesStaticArgs(f)
971	    case S_RewriteFnRef(_, _, sargs) => !sargs.isEmpty
972	    case f: FunctionalRef => !f.getStaticArgs.isEmpty
973	    case SOpExpr(_, f, _) => !f.getStaticArgs.isEmpty
974	    case m: MethodInvocation => !m.getStaticArgs.isEmpty
975	    case _ => false

(* A generic big operator whose static argument a reduction's clause form does not write is instantiated at the reduction's expected type where its result at its bound does not fit that type: the big operator is a call written as an argument of the call that the reduction desugars to. *)
component InferBigOperatorExpectedType
export Executable

trait Red[\T\]
  empty(): T
  join(a: T, b: T): T
end
object Last[\T extends Number\](e: T) extends Red[\T\]
  empty(): T = e
  join(a: T, b: T): T = b
end

opr BIG LAST[\T extends Number\](): Red[\T\] = do
    z: ZZ32 = 0
    Last[\T\](cast[\T\](z))
  end

idt[\T\](x: T): T = x
__bigOperator[\T extends Number\](o: Red[\T\], desugaredClauses: (Red[\T\], T->T)->T): T = desugaredClauses(o, idt[\T\])
__generate[\T extends Number\](g: GeneratorZZ32, r: Red[\T\], f: ZZ32->T): T = do
    var acc: T = r.empty()
    for i <- seq(g) do acc := r.join(acc, f(i)) end
    acc
  end

run(): () = do
    lo: ZZ32 = 1
    n: ZZ32 = 3
    s: ZZ32 = BIG LAST[j <- lo#n] (3 j)

    println("PASS")
  end

end

  def getArgList(arg: Expr): List[Expr] = arg match {

  def partitionArgs(args: List[Expr]): Option[List[Either[Expr, FnExpr]]] = {

    if (partitioned.exists(_.fold(getType(_).isNone, x => false)))
      None
    else
      Some(partitioned)
  }

   * arrow.
   */
  def getArgType(args: List[Either[Expr, FnExpr]]): Type = getArgType(args, NF.typeSpan)

  /** Same as other but provides a location for the span on the new type. */
  def getArgType(args: List[Either[Expr, FnExpr]], span: Span): Type = {
    val argTypes = args.map {
      case Left(e) => getType(e).get
      case Right(_) => Types.BOTTOM_ARROW
    }
    NF.makeMaybeTupleType(span, toJavaList(argTypes))
  }

        tryChecker.tryCheckExpr(unchecked, expectedArrow)

        tryChecker.tryCheckExpr(unchecked, Some(expectedArrow))

(* A big operator whose bound names its own static parameter, in a reduction that writes no static argument, is instantiated at the reduction's declared type where that type fits the bound, and else at the type of the reduction's body; a written static argument wins. *)
component InferBigOperatorSelfBound
export Executable

trait Red[\T\]
  join(a: T, b: T): T
end
object Last[\T extends Equality[\T\]\] extends Red[\T\]
  join(a: T, b: T): T = b
end

opr BIG LAST[\T extends Equality[\T\]\](): Red[\T\] = Last[\T\]

(* The type at which the reduction ran, from the run-time type of its elements. *)
var ran: String = ""
note(x: ZZ32): () = do ran := "ZZ32" end
note(x: ZZ64): () = do ran := "ZZ64" end
note(x: Any): () = do ran := "other" end
unit[\T\](x: T): T = do note(x); x end

object Upto(n: ZZ32) end

__bigOperator[\T extends Equality[\T\]\](o: Red[\T\], desugaredClauses: (Red[\T\], T->T)->T): T = desugaredClauses(o, unit[\T\])
fold[\T\](k: ZZ32, r: Red[\T\], f: ZZ32->T): T =
    if k = 1 then f(1) else r.join(fold[\T\](k - 1, r, f), f(k)) end
__generate[\T\](g: Upto, r: Red[\T\], f: ZZ32->T): T = fold[\T\](g.n, r, f)

kind(x: ZZ32): String = "ZZ32"
kind(x: ZZ64): String = "ZZ64"

lastOf(n: ZZ32): ZZ64 = BIG LAST[j <- Upto(n)] (3 j)

run(): () = do
    s: ZZ32 = BIG LAST[j <- Upto(3)] (3 j)
    assert(s, 9, "s: ZZ32 = BIG LAST[j <- Upto(3)] (3 j), the last of 3, 6 and 9")
    assert(ran, "ZZ32", "a reduction declared ZZ32 over ZZ32 elements runs at ZZ32; Specification/basic/expressions/reductions.tex, section \"Summations and Other Reduction Expressions\"")

    ran := ""
    assert(kind(BIG LAST[j <- Upto(3)] (3 j)), "ZZ32", "a reduction with no declared type takes the type of its body, ZZ32; Specification/basic/expressions/reductions.tex, section \"Summations and Other Reduction Expressions\"")
    assert(ran, "ZZ32", "a reduction with no declared type runs at the type of its body")

    ran := ""
    w: ZZ64 = BIG LAST[j <- Upto(3)] (3 j)
    assert(w = 9, "w: ZZ64 = BIG LAST[j <- Upto(3)] (3 j), the last of 3, 6 and 9")
    assert(ran, "ZZ64", "a reduction declared ZZ64 over ZZ32 elements runs at ZZ64, each element converted; Specification/basic/inference.tex, section \"The Static Arguments of a Call\", the expected type")

    ran := ""
    r: ZZ64 = lastOf(4)
    assert(r = 12, "lastOf(4), a function whose return type ZZ64 is the reduction's declared type")
    assert(ran, "ZZ64", "a reduction that is the body of a function declared to return ZZ64 runs at ZZ64")

    ran := ""
    v: ZZ64 = BIG LAST[\ZZ32\][j <- Upto(3)] (3 j)
    assert(v = 9, "v: ZZ64 = BIG LAST[\\ZZ32\\][j <- Upto(3)] (3 j), the last of 3, 6 and 9")
    assert(ran, "ZZ32", "a written static argument wins over the declared type: the reduction runs at ZZ32 and its value is converted")
    println("PASS")
  end

end
EOF

count[\F extends Object\](b: Box[\F\]): ZZ32 = 1
useOne(g: Box[\ZZ32\] -> ZZ32): ZZ32 = do z: ZZ32 = 7; g(Box[\ZZ32\](z)) end

object Sized[\nat n\](v: ZZ32) end

   * The argument of the call that a reduction with generators desugars to,

   * alone has no instance, as one whose bound names its own static parameter
   * has none. The static argument is the reduction's expected type, where the

   * else the type of the reduction's body. Where neither gives an accepted
   * call, the body's type, or else the expected type, is still written where
   * the big operator has an instance at it, so that the refusal names the
   * reduction's types. None for any other call, and where the big operator has
   * an instance at neither type.

#!/bin/bash
# The gate's distance stage: the compiled checker over the whole interpreter library, the
# fourteen components, the prelude's twelve and the two that List imports, and their apis,
# every stage of every unit run whatever the earlier stages reported, so that nothing hides
# behind an early return; one table.
#
# Why it exists: Pavol's answer 11 (POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-26): the full measurement of the
# distance to the switch-over "becomes a report-only stage of phase 3's gates, whose job is
# driving it down". The checker-count stage beside it (../checker-count/run.sh) sees only
# the errors before each api's early return, 62 of about 1,740 on 2026-09-27.
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir] [setting]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched: the
# shadow sources and classes, the driver, the checker's caches (-Dfortress.caches) and the
# JVM's temporary directory (so Rats! leaves nothing in /tmp) go to the scratch directory
# (default: $TMPDIR or /tmp), and the caches are deleted at the end. It never removes
# /tmp/fortress*rats, which other runs on the machine use. Exit 0 if the table was
# produced, 1 if it could not be. One JVM, -Xmx4g, one busy core: 789 s on the idle 4-CPU
# container on 2026-09-27, 14 to 24 minutes under load 7 to 18 (switch-over-distance-flat.md
# section 5); the table's #seconds and #machine rows say what each run took and where.
#
# The setting: "compile" by default, the compile command's own: DistanceMulti's -setting
# compile takes the extends-Object pre-desugaring from the line that opens
# Shell.useCompilerLibraries() in the tracked ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/Shell.java,
# read at each run (the run stops, with no total, if that line is not there; its "### order="
# line prints the switch it read, extendsObject=...), and turns the compiled-expression
# desugaring on, as the compile path does. Answer 11 names the compile path's setting. That
# line sets the switch off, the implicit bound Any of P-42 (row 412), so the default runs as
# "any", which fixes the switch off whatever Shell.java says; with the switch on, the compile
# setting gave 685 errors on climb batch 22's code, 580 on the bound Object (F-289). "any"
# differs from walk's setting by the compiled-expression desugaring: on the tree of 2026-09-27
# 1,746 to 1,747 errors against 1,737 to 1,738 (FACTS.md, "The true distance to the
# switch-over"). The third argument, any or walk, runs another setting, for a comparison
# with the measurements on file; the gate never passes it.
#
# The overloading checker's memo is off (-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false), as in
# every run of the measurement: keyed on declaration pairs, it hides 27 to 35 errors
# depending on the build order (FACTS.md, "The overloading checker's memo hides errors
# by build order, so every count runs with it off ...").
#
# The sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-27, so that the gate does not
# depend on a probe directory, as the checker-count stage's were: DistanceMulti.java from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance-flat/ (35ef70584); shadow-patch.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/desugar-codegen/ (e5d8cdbd2); add-patch.py and errors.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance/ (a7e3df9ad, 14d2f9839); classify.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/distance-triage/ (e17a9badc); all unchanged but classify.py, which since
# row 577 finds the library places that name three of its classes by their declarations in
# the tree's sources ($FH, passed to table.py), not by line ranges. table.py is new: it
# counts as those scripts count and prints the rows below. The shadow classes are not
# copies: they are made from the tracked sources at every run by text edits that must each
# match exactly once (shadow-patch.py, add-patch.py), so there is no copied checker to go
# stale silently; an edit that no longer matches stops the run before the checker starts,
# and the table then says so in its #shadow row, with no counts.
#
# The table, tab-separated, every row tagged:
#   #distance   the setting, the switches and the fourteen targets
#   #total      distinct errors; or "none:" and why, when no total was measured, as when a
#               target stopped with errors the stage does not count, such as a parse error,
#               or an api that only a later target checks reported errors (table.py)
#   #kind       by kind (errors.py): exclusion, comprises, overloading, return-type, ...
#   #class      by root cause (classify.py, distance-triage.md section 2), with its name
#   #check      a disagreement: errors.py's and table.py's totals, or sites classify.py cannot
#               find in the tree's library source
#   #unit       by the unit that printed the error first
#   #crash      each declaration, stage or target the checker crashed on
#   #seconds    the run's wall time, and FortressLibrary's, the part that takes it
#   #machine    nproc, CPU model and MHz, load at start, JDK, FORTRESS_THREADS
#   #shadow     whether every shadow edit matched the tracked sources; the last row

# distance-flat.md section 5).

case "$SETTING" in any|walk|compile) ;; *) echo "distance: unknown setting $SETTING" >&2 ; exit 1 ;; esac
FLAGS="-Dprobe.tolerant=true -Dprobe.all=true -Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false"
COMPONENTS="Library/FortressLibrary.fss Library/RangeInternals.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss

rm -rf "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp"
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp" \
         "$(dirname "$OUT")" || exit 1
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | sed 's#:[^:]*/default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache##')

MACHINE="nproc=$(nproc); $(grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | sed 's/^[^:]*: *//'); $(grep -m1 'cpu MHz' /proc/cpuinfo | sed 's/^[^:]*: *//') MHz; load at start $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=${FORTRESS_T

#    steps), and the driver; a text edit that no longer matches is the one way this can go stale
SHADOW="every shadow edit matched the tracked sources"
if ! ( cd "$FH" && python3 "$D/shadow-patch.py" ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" \
                && python3 "$D/add-patch.py" "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" ) > "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: a shadow edit no longer matches the tracked sources: $(grep -E '^AssertionError' "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" | tail -1 | tr -s ' ' | cut -c1-200); see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -encoding UTF-8 -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/TypeCheckPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/DesugarPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/CodeGenerationPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/Desugarer.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeComparator.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: the shadow sources no longer compile against the tree; see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/classes" "$D/DistanceMulti.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then

fi

#    the apis that it imports, at any depth, with every stage (DistanceMulti.java's header);
#    an api that only a later target imports, as OneShotFlag's, is checked as the tracked
#    method checks it and prints only its count, which table.py reads

content.content:
# The specification

Three folders hold the team's specification:

- `Specification/` is the team's text, as the revival revises it. It says what the language means, except where a decision of the curator says otherwise.
- `Specification-1.0-frozen/` is the unrevised copy. Cite it as "the Working Draft of February 2011". Only `fortress.1.0.pdf` in it is the 1.0 release. Leave this copy unchanged.
- `Documentation/Specification/` is the team's later restart, which they did not finish. If its Types chapter, `Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick`, covers a topic, cite it beside `Specification/` as the designers' later word.

Appendix I, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, records the changes to the text. Its revival section has one entry for each change that the revival made.

A draft build prints the team's `\note{}` boxes, and a release build hides them. Many say that a feature was not built, for example "Reduction variables are not yet supported." Before you record a missing feature as a gap, grep the notes of its chapter: `grep -n '\\note{' Specification/<file>.tex`.

The api listings of the library part are generated from the library's `.fsi` files when the specification is built (`Specification/library/apis/`, not in the tree). A listing shows the library itself, so it cannot justify a change of the library. Cite the `.fsi` file.

To weigh the specification against the team's later texts, or to find the designers' reason for a rule, read `exploring.md`, "Weighing the sources".

## Changing the text: the revision form

Every change of the text has the four parts below, so that no disagreement between the text and an implementation stays hidden.

1. An entry in the revival section of Appendix I: a `\subsection` with a `\seclabel`. The entry gives:
   - the affected sections, the change, its rationale and its effect. The effect names each departure: each way in which walk or the compiled path does not do what the new text says, with its ledger row.
   - the original text, quoted with its path and line in `Specification-1.0-frozen/`;
   - what a reversal to the alternative not taken would need;

1167:\subsection{Reductions whose element type nothing fixes}
type of a bound such as \TYP{Number} and no instance that applies where the
bound mentions the static parameter itself.
A revision of the interpreter of 9~October 2026 changes the box once more.
It said that ``When no argument of the big operator fixes the element type, the
interpreter takes \TYP{BottomType} for it, and the reduction then accepts no
element''; it now says that where the bound of the big operator's static
parameter mentions the static parameter itself the interpreter leaves that
parameter open and the reduction runs on the types of its elements, an empty
one taking the identity of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, and that until the compiled
type checker directs the desugaring by type a program that both implementations
are to run writes the static argument.
A revision of the interpreter of 14~October 2026 changes the box once more.
It said that ``Neither implementation directs it by type yet'', and that where
the bound of the big operator's static parameter mentions the static parameter
itself ``the interpreter leaves that parameter open'', the reduction running on
the types of its elements ``except that an empty one takes the identity of
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} whatever the type of the expression''; it now says that
neither implementation directs it by the type \VAR{N} of the expression yet,
that the interpreter, which has no static types, instantiates the big operator
by the declared type of the local variable, or the declared return type of the
top-level or local function, whose value the reduction is, otherwise by the
join of the run-time types of its elements, and where
there is none at the bound of its static parameter, or open where that bound
mentions the parameter itself, and that an empty reduction that no declared
type directs takes the identity of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}.
\item[Rationale] The revival decided on 26~September 2026 that the library's
\OPR{SUM} and \OPR{PROD} become generic reductions over the library's algebra,
each joined with its element type's own operator and taking that type's
identity, and that such a clause form writes its static argument, as the team's
own tests do.
Until 9~October 2026 the interpreter took \TYP{BottomType} for the static
parameter of a big operator that no argument fixes (row~424 of the revival's
gap ledger).
The revival decided on 8~October 2026 that the interpreter leaves open a type
parameter whose bound mentions the type parameter itself and that nothing at a
call fixes (\secref{revival-inference}): having no static types, the
interpreter cannot take the type \VAR{N} of the expression, and an open
parameter refuses no element where \TYP{BottomType} refused every one, so that
the reduction runs on the types of its elements, as the desugaring by type
would run it.
Reversing that revision takes one block out of the interpreter's
instantiation of a call and returns such a parameter to \TYP{BottomType}; the
specification's examples that write no static argument for such a reduction
would stop again at their first element, and refusing the call, as the compiled
type checker does, would stop them too.
The revival decided on 14~October 2026 that the interpreter instantiates the
big operator of a reduction or a comprehension that writes no static argument
as the desugaring by the type \VAR{N} would, with run-time types in place of
\VAR{N}: by the declared type of the local variable, or the declared return
type of the top-level or local function, whose value the reduction is, which
constrains the instance as a call's static return type
does (\secref{static-arg-inference}), and otherwise by the join of the
run-time types of its elements, which the interpreter collects before it
reduces them, as it already took the types of the elements for \VAR{N} where
it left the parameter open; with neither, the parameter takes its bound, or is
left open where the bound mentions it.
Until then the interpreter left a big operator's static parameter whose bound
does not mention it at \TYP{BottomType} (\secref{revival-inference}), and an
empty reduction, having no element, took the identity of
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}.
Reversing the revision of 14~October 2026 takes the declared type and the
collection of the elements out of the interpreter's evaluation of such a
reduction and returns those static parameters to \TYP{BottomType}: an empty
reduction of \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} elements then takes the identity of
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} again, the library's set reductions \EXP{\bigcup} and
\EXP{\bigcap} stop again at their first element, a comprehension is built
again at the run-time types of its elements wherever its type is declared, and
the library's \VAR{body} in the application of a big operator can no longer
declare the type of its parameter.
The reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/perf-probes/walk-plain-bound/REPORT.md} and
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-walk-elements/REPORT.md} in the
revival's repository.
The compiled type checker, when it checks the libraries this specification
describes, took \TYP{BottomType} too until it was revised to the rule of
\secref{static-arg-inference} for a type parameter that nothing at a call
fixes; it now takes the parameter's bound, which is not the element type, or,
since 14~October 2026, where the reduction's type at that bound does not fit the
reduction's expected type, that expected type, the big operator being a call
written as an argument of another call (\secref{revival-expected-contexts})
(row~425).
The compiled path's own library declares $\sum$ and
\EXP{\OPR{BIG}\:\OPR{MAX}} for \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} alone, with no static
parameter (\nolinkurl{Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi}, lines 180--184), and
refuses \EXP{\sum\llbracket\mathbb{Z}32\rrbracket [j \gets 0\#4]\: j}
(\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-spec-numbers/probes/skeptic/SkSumClauseTyped.t1.txt}).
\item[Effect] None beyond the box: the forms without a generator clause list need
no static argument.
Since 9~October 2026, under the interpreter, a reduction with a generator clause
list whose element type nothing fixes, over a big operator whose bound mentions
its static parameter, runs where it stopped at its first element, the
specification's examples of that form among them.
Since 14~October 2026, under the interpreter, such a reduction or comprehension
is instantiated by the declared type of its value, by the join of its elements'
run-time types or at its bound: an empty sum that is the value of a function
declared \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} gives the \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} zero, where it gave
the identity of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} (row~645 of the revival's gap ledger), the
library's set reductions \EXP{\bigcup} and \EXP{\bigcap} run where they
stopped at their first element (row~662), and a comprehension that is the
value of a local variable or of a top-level or local function declared with its
type is built at that type.
An empty reduction that no declared type directs still gives the identity of
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} whatever the type of the expression, and an empty
comprehension is built at its big operator's bound (row~716); a
comprehension that no declared type reaches, such as the value of a top-level
variable, a field or a method, or the body of another reduction, is built at
the run-time types of its elements (rows~20 and~717). Since 16~October 2026 a
reduction over a big operator whose declared result is a trait other than the
library's \TYP{BigReduction}, \TYP{Comprehension} and \TYP{BigOperator} is
instantiated through the one of those three that the trait extends, its static
arguments put for the trait's, as one declared with that supertype is (row~718).
The compiled type checker still refuses that form (row~425).
\item[Original text] Unchanged.
\item[Route C] The same under route~C.
\end{description}

content.content:
# Committing and pushing

**scratch**
: Files and folders that your work makes and `main` does not keep: logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, probe programs, lists and private caches folders.

Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.

## What to commit

- Commit your change, its tests, your report if it is a file, and any reusable script.
- Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records. A row's close follows the fix's commit (`records.md`).
- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
- In a fresh clone, `.claude/worktrees/` and `.claude/agents/` show as untracked, because the lines of `.git/info/exclude` that hide them are not in the clone. Do not commit them.
- Keep a copyrighted PDF or deck in `research/decks/`, which is gitignored. Cite it by its Wayback URL. Notes on it go in `research/extracts/`: your own summary, with brief attributed quotations.
- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.
- Name a model by its tier (Opus, Sonnet, Fable) in any text that you commit, commit messages included. Never write its model identifier, the API's name for the model, which starts with `claude-`.

## How to commit

Commit as you go, each commit in one command that names its paths:

    git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>

- The command commits only the paths that it names. Other agents may have uncommitted edits in your tree. Leave them alone.
- If you renamed a file with `git mv`, name its old path in `git commit` only, because `git add` refuses a path that no longer exists: `git add -- <new paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <new paths> <old paths>`.
- Never commit a copied directory, and never use `git add -A`.
- Before you commit more than a few hundred lines, stage them and read what you staged: `git add -- <paths> && git diff --cached --stat -- <paths>`.
- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests:

      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB

  If your brief gives another session line, use it. If a commit that is already made has a footer that names a model, by any name or identifier, leave the commit as it is. Such a footer is not a defect: do not check for it, report it or list it.

## Pushing

Push after every commit, so that a lost container loses nothing.

- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`. Your brief says how the branch reaches `main`.
- From a session in a cloud container, do not try to delete a branch on GitHub, or retry a refusal with another tool (the `cloud-container` skill, "Rules for every agent"). Removing a worktree does not delete its branch, which stays. Ask nobody in your report to delete a branch.
- If you work on `main`, other agents commit to it too. Push only your own commits:
  1. Run `git log origin/main..main`. Your commits are those whose hashes your own `git commit` printed.
  2. If it lists another agent's commit, run the command again shortly: that agent pushes right after it commits. If the commit stays, push nothing, and say so in your report.
  3. If it lists only your commits, push the three refs with this one command, and wait for it to end:

         git push --atomic origin main main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8 main:blinded-fable

     With `--atomic`, the three refs update together or not at all. Do not pipe the command into another command, since a pipe hides a refusal. A refusal shows as a line that starts with `!`, and as a non-zero exit. The last ref keeps `blinded-fable` current. If the container is lost, the platform rebuilds it from that branch.
- Push no branch that this section does not name, unless your brief names it.
- If a push is refused, push nothing more, and do not run it again. Report the refused ref and git's message.

content.content:
\subsection{Reductions whose element type nothing fixes}
\seclabel{revival-reductions}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected section] \secref{reduction-expr}.
\item[Change] One box after the first sentence says that neither implementation
directs the desugaring of a reduction by type yet, so a reduction with a
generator clause list whose element type no argument fixes writes its static
argument; and that until the compiled path is built on the libraries this
specification describes, it compiles against a smaller library of its own,
whose big operators take no static argument and range over \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}
only, so that there the clause form runs without its static argument and a
written one is refused. The normative text is unchanged.
The box said at first that ``the interpreter, and the compiled type checker
when it checks the libraries this specification describes, each take
\TYP{BottomType} for it, and the reduction then accepts no element''; it now
says that the interpreter does, and that the compiled type checker takes the
bound of the big operator's static parameter, which gives the reduction the
type of a bound such as \TYP{Number} and no instance that applies where the
bound mentions the static parameter itself.
30:Neither implementation directs it by the type \VAR{N} of the expression yet.

''')

old='''mentions the parameter itself, and that an empty reduction that no declared
type directs takes the identity of \\EXP{\\mathbb{Z}32}.
\\item[Rationale] The revival decided on 26~September 2026 that the library's
'''

new='''mentions the parameter itself, and that an empty reduction that no declared
type directs takes the identity of \\EXP{\\mathbb{Z}32}.
A revision of the compiled type checker of 15~November 2026 changes the box
once more.

static parameter, which is not the element type, or, where the reduction's
type at that bound does not fit the reduction's expected type, that expected
type'', that ``a bound that mentions the static parameter itself gives no
instance that applies, so that the reduction is refused (row~425)'', and that
``Until the compiled type checker directs the desugaring by type, a reduction
with a generator clause list whose element type no argument fixes writes its
static argument in a program that both implementations are to run''; it now
says that the compiled type checker takes the bound where the reduction so
instantiated is accepted and its type fits the expected type, and otherwise
instantiates the big operator by the reduction's expected type, where the
reduction is then accepted, and else by the type of the reduction's body; that
the two implementations differ where the expected type comes from a place that
the interpreter does not read; and that a reduction writes its static argument
where they would so differ.
Its sentence ``Neither implementation directs it by the type \\VAR{N} of the
expression yet'' now says that neither desugars a reduction by that type yet,
each instantiating the big operator that the reduction names.
\\item[Rationale] The revival decided on 26~September 2026 that the library's
'''
s=s.replace(old,new)
# 2. Rationale: after the sentence ending (row~425). in the compiled checker paragraph
old='''reduction's expected type, that expected type, the big operator being a call
written as an argument of another call (\\secref{revival-expected-contexts})
(row~425).
'''
assert s.count(old)==1
new=old+'''Since 15~November 2026 it instantiates the big operator of a reduction with a
generator clause list that writes no static argument, where the reduction is
not accepted with the big operator at its bound, by the reduction's expected
type, and otherwise by the type of the reduction's body: the type \\VAR{N} of
the expression, by which this specification directs the desugaring, is the
expected type where the context gives one and the elements convert to it, and
otherwise the type of the body.
The expected type goes first so that the two implementations sum alike a
reduction that is the value of a local variable declared with a type or of a
function declared with a return type, where the interpreter instantiates the
big operator by that type since 14~October 2026: with the body's type first, a
sum of \\EXP{\\mathbb{Z}32} elements that is the value of a local variable
declared \\EXP{\\mathbb{R}64} would be summed in \\EXP{\\mathbb{Z}32} when compiled
and in \\EXP{\\mathbb{R}64} under the interpreter.
A reduction that is accepted with the big operator at its bound is unchanged,
so that no reduction that the compiled type checker accepted before invokes
another instance.
Reversing this revision takes the reduction's own check out of the compiled
type checker's check of an application; a reduction over $\\sum$, $\\prod$,
\\EXP{\\OPR{BIG}\\:\\OPR{MIN}} or \\EXP{\\OPR{BIG}\\:\\OPR{MAX}} that writes no
static argument is then refused again.
The reasoning is in
\\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-static-argument-inferred/REPORT.md}
in the revival's repository.
'''
s=s.replace(old,new)
# 3. Effect's last sentence
old='''arguments put for the trait's, as one declared with that supertype is (row~718).
The compiled type checker still refuses that form (row~425).
'''
assert s.count(old)==1
new='''arguments put for the trait's, as one declared with that supertype is (row~718).
Since 15~November 2026 the compiled type checker accepts a reduction with a
generator clause list that writes no static argument over a big operator whose
bound mentions its static parameter, as the bounds of $\\sum$, $\\prod$,
\\EXP{\\OPR{BIG}\\:\\OPR{MIN}} and \\EXP{\\OPR{BIG}\\:\\OPR{MAX}} do, which it
refused until then (row~425): it instantiates the big operator by the
reduction's expected type, its elements converted, or else by the type of the
reduction's body, as the box says, and likewise a comprehension whose type at
its big operator's bound does not fit the declared type of its value.
Where the expected type comes from a method's declared return type, a field,
a top-level variable, an assignment or a parameter, the interpreter, which
reads none of these, still instantiates the big operator by the join of its
elements' run-time types and converts the value after (row~NEW-C-2).
The compiled type checker still refuses such a reduction over a big operator
with two or more static parameters that nothing fixes, as
\\EXP{\\OPR{BIG}\\:\\OPR{MIN\\_MAX}} (row~NEW-C-1).
'''
s=s.replace(old,new)
# 4. revival-expected-contexts Effect
old='''fit it; it is refused as before where the big operator has no instance at its
bound, as one whose bound mentions its own static parameter has none
(row~425).
'''
assert s.count(old)==1
new='''fit it; until 15~November 2026 it was refused where the big operator has no
instance at its bound, as one whose bound mentions its own static parameter
has none (row~425), and it is now instantiated by the reduction's expected
type, or else by the type of its body (\\secref{revival-reductions}).
'''
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
EOF
